author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Playstation 2 Startup Sound Explained
summary: Nitrocosm separates the PS2 startup sequence into its main chord, BIOS-held samples and later status sounds, while crediting original composer Takafumi Fujisawa and acknowledging a visible specification typo in the video.

blocks.text: The chapter list gives the four-minute explanation a useful structure: a technical overview leads into the familiar startup sound, then the BIOS and constituent audio samples, before the post-startup cues are interpreted separately. This avoids treating every noise in the sequence as one static recording. The description also credits Takafumi Fujisawa and links a deeper reconstruction of the “piano smashing” chord. Together, those elements connect authored sound design to the console state changes players learned to recognize.

The creator explicitly notes that some displayed CPU-spec numbers gained an erroneous letter, so the video should not be cited for those labels without correction. It also mentions copyrighted BIOS-contained samples but refuses to redistribute them; the Hub entry likewise provides no BIOS or extracted audio. The explanation is a compact sound-design analysis, not official Sony documentation of every cue or an instruction to obtain protected firmware. Attribution and functional interpretations should be cross-checked against primary interviews where available.
